#5095. Want Studio-Style Pilates at Home? Start With These Editor-Tested Reformers

Our top picks for every kind of at-home Pilates setup, from compact machines to studio-worthy reformers.

Women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

If you’re a pilates princess, you already know what a reformer is, and you’re well acquainted with the many ways it delivers a low-impact, strength-building workout. However, if you’re a newbie, here’s a quick crash course: A reformer is a specially designed machine, originally developed by Joseph Pilates, that consists of springs for resistance, a moving carriage, a foot bar that you push or pull, and pulleys to hold onto or hook to your feet when performing pilates exercises.

“I’d describe the reformer as a machine designed to help create an understanding of your body with resistance,” says Sam Miles, owner and co-founder of Good Time Pilates in New York City. “It gives real time feedback so you can find sensation through the shortening and lengthening of your muscles. In short and easy terms: an assist to finding your muscle engagement!”

There are unique benefits to using a reformer that are hard to replicate in a pilates mat workout, or really any other type of workout. But that doesn’t mean you have to be advanced to start using one. “The modifications to increase or decrease challenge make it a truly universal machine for any body and any fitness level, which is very unique and just awesome,” Miles says. “You can rehabilitate with a reformer, strengthen muscles, stretch and find release work, it’s the best!”

Pilates reformers are available in different types: classical and contemporary. The classical reformer stays true to Joseph Pilates’ original design; the machines are made of wood, and have springs that all have the exact same resistance level. Purists are going to want to consider these machines.

Contemporary reformers are an evolutionary riff on the original and often incorporate springs of varying resistance that can be adjusted. The dimensions also usually vary a bit from the OG classical reformer design.

While it used to be that reformers were only found in Pilates studios, more and more women are investing in a reformer as an addition to their home gym setup. There are also less intense reformer models on the market that are specifically designed for at-home use, and these generally come in at a fraction of the cost of a classical or studio-grade contemporary reformer.

After testing a bunch of options, we narrowed down our picks to a variety of machines, including commercial-grade reformers and pared-down, reimagined reformers that are made specifically to take up less space and be more affordable.

After testing a handful of Pilates reformers, the contemporary-style Balanced Body Allegro 2 came out on top for its studio-quality, strong springs, durable build, and versatile foot bar. WH fitness contributor Talene Appleton has been using it two to three times a week to practice at home for almost two years, and it’s still in mint condition. Appleton says it’s built like a tank and is commercial-grade, so it’s the best you can get for your at-home gym setup.

Five springs are featured for varying tension to accommodate different levels—three high resistance (red), one medium resistance (blue), and one light resistance (yellow), while the steel, grippy foot bar glides effortlessly for 10 vertical and horizontal positions. “I was blown away by how much the additional positions of its foot bar allowed me to change up my usual Pilates sequences,” says Appleton. “This adds incredible versatility in terms of movement options that most competitors can’t beat.” While the foot bar is its best feature, Appleton notes it’s the most difficult to set up and requires two people to line it up evenly on each side.Appleton says this machine is best for advanced users, given there’s a bit of a learning curve at first. “Using a traditional reformer at home can be a bit overwhelming at first, especially if you’re used to having an instructor call the shots in terms of spring resistance, foot bar positions, moves, and all the rest,” she says. “I found myself second-guessing my setup and wondering if I was getting the most out of each exercise (or sometimes if the move I was doing was even a real exercise at all).” She credits YouTube and TikTok tutorials for guiding her along, specifically from Balanced Body and East River Pilates.While this is the best Pilates machine money can buy (with a steep price tag of $4,345 *sigh*) it’s heavy at 157 pounds. It’s also large, at eight feet long and three feet wide, so make sure you have adequate space before splurging. It’s also not the easiest to set up. “Setting this thing up was no joke—I knew I was in for a challenge when I saw the multiple massive, heavy boxes it arrived in,” Appleton says. She notes it took her and a friend two hours to assemble.

Read More: Balanced Body Allegro 2 Review

The classical Merrithew At Home SPX Reformer is next-level if you want to up your Pilates game. It features a foldable vertical tower, which can improve flexibility and target different muscle groups with more controlled movements, adding more challenge. It has five springs—four full-resistance and one with half-resistance. Given the springs mostly have the same resistance, this machine is designed for more advanced users.

The foot bar is adjustable with four positions for different heights, while the carriage is padded for comfort. Another call-out is the included reformer box, which adds height and range of motion to moves in the seated and lying position. It’s especially helpful for those with muscle tightness or who need to modify moves involving the knees.

While this is a great reformer to elevate your practice, it’s quite large at 96 inches long and 26 inches wide. It’s also heavy at 115 pounds. Like the AeroPilates Pro XP 557, this isn’t ideal for apartments. The tower structure also requires more vertical space, so if you don’t have high ceilings, our best overall is most likely your best bet.

Read More: Best Compact Home Gym Equipment

Pretty much all pilates reformers in this guide are relatively large, but the contemporary AeroPilates Reformer 4420 is foldable. If you’re an apartment dweller, this machine is your compact answer to your Pilates reformer dreams. It can be stashed under a couch, bed, or behind a door. At 69 pounds, it’s not the lightest, so having two people for setup is probably your best bet.

Like the AeroPilates Reformer 287, it uses cords, not springs, yet delivers impressive effectiveness. This model has four adjustable cords with varying resistances and color codes, unlike the 287: two standard resistances (black), one extra intensity (red), and one light resistance (yellow). So, this reformer is good for both beginners and those who are more advanced.

It also has a built-in cardio rebounder, which is essentially a mini trampoline at the foot bar, making it an especially good choice for someone looking for low-impact cardio options and variety.

The contemporary Your Reformer is studio-grade like our best overall reformer pick, and is super durable despite being a little over half the price. During a stay in Los Angeles, Appleton rented one for at-home workouts and was extremely impressed with its easily changeable five thick springs, and a carriage that glides smoothly and quietly. The springs are also color-coded: two heavy resistance (red), two medium resistance (blue), and one light resistance (yellow).

In terms of quality, it’s a direct competitor to the Allegro 2. “The straps are thick and definitely won’t fray on me, and the strap handles are comfortable to grip, even when my palms get sweaty,” Appleton says. It’s not compact enough for most apartments, but it’s slimmer to accommodate home spaces better.

Appleton is 5’5” and found the carriage to be wide and spacious, with plenty of room to move around from supine to standing to kneeling positions. It also accommodates her much taller boyfriend, who’s “20 times more passionate about a good reformer workout,” so it’s the real deal.

The AeroPilates Reformer 287 is the most affordable option we’ve come across. It’s dramatically less expensive than our best overall—it costs under $400! But that doesn’t mean it’s less effective. Its quality is still impressive, just not studio-grade. WH entertainment editor Amy Wilkinson, an avid Pilates practitioner, was surprised by how sturdy this machine is because of its bargain price, and since it comes pre-assembled (another plus).

But, she stresses it’s best for beginners since it only features three resistance cords. “I could see someone eventually progressing beyond the capabilities of this model, especially when it comes to exercises like footwork and running, which are classically done on four springs,” says Wilkinson. “It also lacks certain accessories you’d typically find with a studio machine—a box, which is typically used for exercises in the short-box series and in a long position for pulling straps and T-press, among others.”

Speaking of resistance, unlike our best overall, this reformer uses cords instead of springs. While they can be trickier to hook on and off, their weight is identical to springs Wilkinson uses on studio-grade models.The carriage glides smoothly, although Wilkinson notes the attached handles would fall and get in the way. She recommends tossing them aside instead of hanging on the built-in shoulder blocks. As for the foot bar, it’s stable but can’t be adjusted for specific exercises.Aside from mechanics, this reformer is extremely compact, weighing just 56 pounds, and measuring 42 inches when folded and 85 inches fully extended. Wilkinson lives in a one-bedroom Brooklyn apartment and has no issues stashing it away, although she finds it tricky to fold and wide when the foot bar is attached.AeroPilates says this product can fit people up to 6'4", but Wilkinson, who is 5’11”, says even her height was pushing the machine’s limits. “I imagine anyone much taller than I am would feel a bit crunched,” she says. She also says it’s narrow, and didn’t have additional breathing room.

While most full-sized pilates reformers don’t have a built-in trampoline at the foot bar, the contemporary AeroPilates Pro XP 557 is the first full-sized model we’ve seen with a rebounder, so cardio moves like single-leg pushups and slow squats can be added to the routine. This is especially useful for beginners getting into the groove. WH associate visual editor Berkeley Brooks found it stayed sturdy when executing explosive movements at fast paces, while the material of the main carriage prevented her from slipping around.

Brooks notes that the four strong springs are easily interchangeable and have varying resistances labeled by color: two low resistance (blue) and two high resistance (yellow). The foot bar is adjustable, thick, and quiet for added comfort, and can be placed in three positions to accommodate different heights without disrupting your range of motion.

The platform is also wide at 23 inches and long at 100 inches, so this model isn’t ideal for small apartments, especially since you need additional space to execute exercises.

On the upside, Brooks says it’s easy to build and aesthetically pleasing. “I love the addition of wood to the machine because it looks great in a home gym,” she adds.

The springs in a pilates reformer are an important consideration when you’re choosing your machine. “Springs provide resistance and feedback, so the type and responsiveness of springs deeply influence your experience,” says Mo Wolfe, owner and Pilates instructor of Evolution Pilates in Port Washington, New York.

The weight of springs can also depend on whether a machine is classical or contemporary. Classical style reformers have a heavier spring tension that is the same throughout, while modern models generally tend to offer springs with a variety of resistance levels. A reformer with springs is the type you’ll find in a Pilates studio.

Alternatively, resistance cords are sometimes used in the place of springs in reformer machines that are designed for personal and at-home use. They offer similar effectiveness and are more affordable.

Taking the size of your home into consideration is important before purchasing a Pilates machine. Not only do you want to make sure you have enough room for the machine itself, you also want to make sure there will be enough space to perform the full range of Pilates reformer exercises, like leg circles, that require room to move.

Some reformers are very big and bulky, such as our pro-level, best overall selection. They take up considerable real estate and they’re best for a home gym where they can become a more permanent fixture that won’t need to be moved once it’s installed.

If your workout space is multi-functional (i.e., it’s your living room) and your equipment needs to have a smaller footprint and be more portable so you can move it around or stash it away, look for a lighter, foldable option. Just make sure that you’ll have enough space to do the moves when it’s all set up.

Since reformer Pilates is a low-impact activity, and the resistance can be so fine-tuned for your fitness level, there are no hard and fast rules about how often you do a reformer session each week. Miles says it really comes down to how your body feels. “With the variety you can get from a reformer, daily use is manageable. At my studio we have challenging classes, stretch and release classes, technique-focused classes; variety is important!” She notes that most of her clients do three reformer sessions per week.

We picked the brains of Pilates instructors to understand what to look for when shopping for a reformer, then researched dozens of the top-rated models. From there, Women’s Health writers and editors (including fitness contributors Nicolette Accardi and Talene Appleton, and entertainment editor Amy Wilkinson) tested some of the best themselves to narrow down the options.

During testing, they paid close attention to spring and cord resistance level as a measure of whether or not the machines were ideal for beginners or more advanced users. The testers also considered size, durability, and ease of assembly to determine what sorts of spaces were needed for these machiness. Moves like planks, triceps presses, running (pushing off the foot bar), chest expansions, and leg circles were all completed during our testing Pilates workouts to really put these machine to the test.

*Additional reporting by Nicolette Accardi.

#5093. Diesel prices plunge 8%, yet Bitcoin traders face a squeeze

October’s PPI slowed at the headline level, but higher freight prices and firm underlying inflation leave financing relief uncertain.

US wholesale inflation slowed in October, but rising freight prices and firm underlying pressure complicate the case that cheaper fuel will make financing easier for Bitcoin (BTC) holders while BTC remains below $70,000.

The Bureau of Labor Statistics’ October producer-price report, released Nov. 13, showed diesel prices falling 7.9% as truck freight prices rose 3.9%. Headline wholesale inflation slowed sharply, but the measure excluding food, energy, and trade services kept rising at September’s monthly pace.

Final-demand PPI rose 0.3% in October, seasonally adjusted, after September’s revised 1.4% increase.

The measure excluding food, energy and trade services rose 0.5% for a second month. Its annual increase eased to 4.9% from 5%, while headline annual PPI accelerated to 6.5% from 6.3%. Those readings support a mixed assessment of some comparisons improved, but underlying monthly pressure held firm.

BLS attributed more than 80% of October’s 0.2% rise in final-demand services prices to truck freight. Transportation and warehousing services rose 2%, even as final-demand energy prices slipped 0.1%. Goods prices increased 0.5%.

Cheaper diesel coexisted with higher prices for moving goods. For now, the freight increase undercuts an assumption that a lower fuel bill immediately means cheaper transport.

Unprocessed intermediate goods prices fell 3.1%. Alongside slower monthly headline inflation and the easing annual exclusion measure, that gives the more optimistic interpretation real evidence. The question is whether that cooling broadens and lasts.

Diesel and truck freight moved in opposite directions in October. The inflation picture also changes with the comparison window.

September → October 2026: headline PPI slowed; the measure excluding food, energy and trade services stayed at 0.5%.

September → October 2026: annual headline PPI rose from 6.3% to 6.5%; the exclusion measure eased from 5.0% to 4.9%.

Fuel relief coexists with firm underlying monthly inflation; annual readings are mixed.

PPI series describe different producer prices. Concurrent diesel and freight changes do not establish cause or pass-through timing. Monthly changes are seasonally adjusted; annual changes are unadjusted. PPI is distinct from CPI and PCE.

Reported BLS figures. Main signed bars share a linear −10% to +5% axis. Panel bars start at zero, with monthly scale 0–1.5% and annual scale 0–7%. September monthly figures use the release's revisions. No causal or policy effect is calculated.

PPI series describe different producer prices. Concurrent diesel and freight changes do not establish cause or pass-through timing. Monthly changes are seasonally adjusted; annual changes are unadjusted. PPI is distinct from CPI and PCE.

PPI measures the selling prices domestic producers receive, CPI measures prices paid by consumers, while the Fed targets inflation measured by personal consumption expenditures (PCE).

The measures overlap in the economic pressures they describe, but their readings are not interchangeable.

Speaking before that day’s CPI release, Fed Governor Christopher Waller leaned toward further tightening through a 25-basis-point December rate increase if conditions developed as expected.

He said a 50-basis-point increase should be considered if October core CPI resembled the previous two readings around 0.3% or higher.

The subsequent CPI report showed a 0.4% monthly headline increase and a third consecutive 0.3% increase excluding food and energy.

The Fed’s explanation of monetary policy describes how policy-rate changes affect short-term interest rates and broader financial conditions. Applied to Bitcoin, the conditional mechanism is that lower financing costs could make borrowed exposure easier to carry, while easier conditions could encourage investors to allocate more to risk.

The route from producer prices to financing relief remains conditional. Persistent inflation could keep policy restrictive even when one fuel price falls, while a recovery case based on financing relief needs evidence beyond cheaper diesel.

Farside Investors' completed Nov. 12 row records US Bitcoin ETF net outflows of $284.1 million, preceding the PPI release.

ETF flows describe one investment channel. Still, completed inflows would provide firmer evidence of buyers returning than an inflation-based expectation alone.

Broader cooling in consumer and producer prices, less restrictive assessments from policymakers and observable financing relief would strengthen the case that fuel declines are becoming useful for Bitcoin holders.

Sustained ETF inflows would add demand evidence, while continued underlying inflation pressure and further withdrawals would keep that case weaker, even if diesel keeps getting cheaper.

#5092. SoFi Brings Its Bank-Issued Stablecoin to Polygon’s Payments Stack

SoFi Brings Its Bank-Issued Stablecoin to Polygon’s Payments Stack

SoFi is widening the reach of its digital dollar, bringing SoFiUSD, the first stablecoin issued by a U.S. national bank, onto Polygon’s payments infrastructure as banks and fintechs push stablecoins deeper into everyday money movement.

Polygon Labs said Thursday that SoFiUSD is now live on Polygon Open Money Stack, a payments layer that bundles fiat on- and off-ramps, embedded wallets and cross-chain settlement into a single integration.

The move adds Polygon alongside Ethereum and Solana, the networks SoFiUSD already runs on, and lets SoFi’s more than 17 million members buy, sell, hold, and convert the token on Polygon directly in the SoFi app, without opening a separate crypto wallet or manually bridging assets between chains.

“SoFi is well positioned to bring stablecoins into mainstream finance because it combines the regulatory foundation of a national bank with the reach of a major consumer and enterprise technology platform,” said Marc Boiron, CEO of Polygon Labs.

The expansion lands as stablecoins move beyond crypto trading into the plumbing used to settle card payments, pay businesses, and send money across borders.

On Polygon Open Money Stack, SoFiUSD joins USDC, USDT and PayPal’s PYUSD, and can connect to the wallets, banking rails, and local currencies businesses need for payouts, settlement and cross-border transfers, opening up uses well beyond consumer trading.

The token is redeemable one-to-one for U.S. dollars and issued by SoFi Bank, which is regulated by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency.

SoFi launched SoFiUSD late last year across Ethereum and Solana as the first stablecoin from a U.S. national bank, and it already settles the company’s entire card program over Mastercard’s network. The firm has been building out a broader digital-money suite, recently launching SoFi Earn, a tokenized deposit that pays 4.40% yield and converts one-to-one into SoFiUSD.

For Polygon, the addition deepens a payments business that has become one of the network’s calling cards.

Polygon recently extended Open Money Stack to Solana, and the chain has processed more than $3 trillion in lifetime stablecoin transfer volume, according to the company. Visa and Mastercard support stablecoin settlement on Polygon, while Stripe uses it to route USDC payments for merchants in more than 150 countries.

SoFiUSD is a payment stablecoin, not a bank deposit, and is not FDIC- or SIPC-insured, bank-guaranteed or legal tender.

#5087. US courts target $1.2B in stolen Binance funds, yet victims face a new hurdle

DOJ secured court authority over $1.2 billion from Binance’s $6 billion hack, with forfeiture and repayment timelines unresolved.

US authorities have secured court authorization to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion stolen from Binance funds, advancing the legal effort to recover assets from the October theft.

The Department of Justice (DOJ) disclosed the authorization on Nov. 12 but did not announce completed forfeiture or a timetable for returning the money.

The court-covered assets sit within more than $2.7 billion frozen through combined US government and private-sector efforts, according to the department.

The larger figure measures the combined freezing effort, while the smaller one identifies the portion for which DOJ reports seizure or restraint authority.

Binance had already committed to covering its losses in its Nov. 3 incident report. The exchange promised to absorb the financial impact of the stolen funds and said it had set aside more than 100% of what it would need to cover the loss.

DOJ attributes the theft of more than $6 billion on or about Oct. 29 to North Korean military actors known as TraderTraitor. Its announcement said efforts to trace, freeze, seize and forfeit the stolen assets remained ongoing as the attackers continued laundering them through cryptocurrency bridges, mixers and exchanges.

#5085. 9 Best At-Home Laser Hair Removal Devices of 2026, Tested by Women's Health Editors

Our favorites include Braun and Epilaser.

Women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

Fall is in full swing, but if you’re like us and prefer a smooth look year-round, you’ve likely tried all sorts of hair removal tools. Disposable razors are convenient, but dermatologist Caroline Robinson, MD, says they can cause microscopic nicks and irritation. Waxing provides immediate results, but the upkeep and the pain of simultaneously ripping out dozens of hairs from our legs are as painful as they sound. Enter at-home laser hair removal devices, which dermatologists and our hard-to-please editors swear by for their legs, bikini lines, underarms, and faces.

They zap unwanted hairs at their roots, significantly slowing regrowth and leaving skin smoother. While they don’t offer permanent hair loss, we’ve found the long-term effects are worth using one of these devices. After testing them for more than three years, we’re confident that you’ll also enjoy the long-term results they deliver. Most of these devices take anywhere from one to four weeks for initial results, and up to 12 weeks for full results to show. Starting now gives you enough time to ensure that you’re hair-free by your next vacation to these Travel Award-winning destinations.

Need more motivation to start now? It’ll take four weeks for visible results to show, which means if you start now, then you’ll notice a difference before your holiday travel, with better results by the time you enjoy a gorgeous fall wedding. So start your at-home laser hair removal treatments now, stay consistent, and by the time your next beach trip hits, you’ll forget what shaving even feels like.

So what makes laser hair removal devices worthy of a spot in your busy routine? They have an upfront time commitment: you have to initially use one up to five times a week. But after a few months, your upkeep routine drops significantly to once or twice each season. They’re also more cost-effective than professional treatments. Hear us out: A laser that costs $500 is basically the same price as a professional hair removal session, and the results from that in-office treatment won't last forever, but you will continue using your at-home laser for years.

Ahead, we asked seven dermatologists about how to shop for laser hair removal devices and their no-fail product recommendations. They also answered your most burning questions in our FAQ section after our product highlights.

Meet the Skin I-Expert, a Braun laser hair removal device that we’ve been testing since January 2024. Given our long-term positive experience using this tool, we knew it was the clear winner of our best overall distinction.

For starters, most laser hair removal devices have about 200,000 flashes or the equivalent of 780 at-home treatments, Dr. Nazarian previously told us in our guide to the best facial hair removal devices. This IPL device has double that, aka 1,560 treatments, meaning the investment will last for several years even with consistent use. Each hair removal sesh will only cost you $0.31, which is a third of the price of a Wet n Wild eyeliner.

Next, it’s our only recommended device that connects to a compatible smartphone app via Bluetooth and Wi-Fi technology to tailor your treatment to your needs. Wohlner was impressed with how well the intuitive app assessed her skin tone and hair color for compatibility.

Wohlner admits that she never used interchangeable heads before because they were intimidating. However, Braun solved that problem because the app told her what head to use for different parts of her body. The software even analyzes how much coverage Wohlner needs to ensure she doesn't miss any spots. Lastly, the app has a built-in calendar, so she’ll always remember when she’s due for some zaps—something Wohlner admits can be hard to keep track of, but is key for results.

Like other Braun laser hair removal devices we've tried, this one comes in a sturdy carrying case that keeps everything neatly organized under your vanity, or wherever you choose to store it. The unit doesn't call out any specific cooling technology, but Wohlner said her experience was largely pain-free. "I felt a little zippiness here and there, but nothing I could actually describe as painful—more like a super quick, tiny pinch," she says.

As for the results, they were solid. Wohlner typically shaves her self-described super coarse hair daily until she started using this device. She was impressed that she didn’t need to shave her underarms for weeks after her first treatment. "After three more sessions, I saw a pretty major payoff,” says Wohlner. “There are definitely a few hairs still popping through, but they've grown back so slowly."

Overall, this device is pricey, but for someone serious about tackling the hair on their body—whether armpits, legs, Brazilian area, and beyond—it's worth every penny, especially if you feel like you could use a little help through the process.

Truly the only thing we don’t enjoy about this device is the price tag. However, it has 400,000 flashes—double the average of our other favorite devices—which means this Braun can easily last you 30 years. Genius!

If you can't stomach the price of Braun's latest and greatest IPL, the brand’s cheaper Silk Expert Pro 5 is hardly a downgrade. In our comprehensive test, Earley found the device to be both easy to use and highly effective.

The Silk Expert Pro 5 removes all of Earley’s unwanted hair after just four weeks of use. "I was so happy to say goodbye to my leg and armpit hair,” says the working mom of four. “Anything that saves me time—and trust me, not having to shave is a huge time-saver—is something I'm 100% willing to invest in." The ergonomic handle is easier to hold than the bulky, cheaper alternatives that remind her of hair dryers. For larger areas of her body, Earley holds down the trigger for continuous flashes—a feature she says speeds things up immensely.

Compared to our best overall pick, the Silk Expert Pro 5 lacks convenience features like a compatible smartphone app that allows you to tailor your treatments and track coverage areas to make sure you don't miss any spots. It does, however, have a proprietary SensoAdapt technology, which uses a built-in sensor to continuously and automatically read your skin tone and self-adjust the energy setting for safety and efficacy just like its more expensive counterpart.

Overall, it's a worthy pick—as evidenced by Earley’s testing experience and its popularity on Amazon and TikTok—if you're looking to spend a little bit less and don't mind sacrificing a few features.

We’ve been testing and liking Ulike devices since 2022. From the ULike Sapphire Air+ to the Air 3, and now the featured Air 10 is the brand’s latest model worth owning.

Instead of buying two devices, the Air 10 works quite literally from your face to your toes. The latest version is equipped with dual lights to zap hair on your upper lip, bikini area, underarms, and legs. It offers four modes, including a new setting for stubborn hairs. The gentle intensity setting zaps hair from the face, while the strongest mode uses high-speed flashes to speed up removing unwanted face and body hair.

What we like most is that Air 10 is easy to use and relatively pain-free. While other devices use heat to remove hair, the Ulike Air 10 cools itself down to 65 degrees Fahrenheit. This chilly surface helps lower your skin temperature to prevent irritation and burns from overheating. Maberry says the cooling tech found in both the Air 3 and Air 10 models is especially useful for sensitive areas like the bikini line.

It’s also a relatively low time commitment of 20 to 30 minutes for a full treatment while watching TV. "Once you get the hang of how to use the device, it's super easy to zap, zap, zap while you scroll through TikTok,” Maberry said in her review. Ulike promises visible results within four weeks, but Maberry saw her hair thin in just three weeks. The hair-free appearance was so dramatic around week six that Maberry was tempted to stop the treatments entirely. She continued using it for the recommended 12 weeks and now hairs only pop up every four to six weeks.

One thing to note: the built-in cooling fan is a bit noisy, so Maberry turns up her TV volume slightly. Still, the tradeoff isn’t a real dealbreaker: "I would rather have a painless device that makes little noise than a silent one that causes a burning sensation," she said. It’s also worth mentioning that this device is best suited for someone with fair to olive complexions and brown to black hair. The tech can’t accurately differentiate between a deeper skin tone and dark tresses.

This budget-conscious device seems a little too good to be true, but it earned a casual 4-star average from nearly 12,900 Amazon reviews. More than 7,330 of these reviews are a perfect 5-star rating. Not too shabby! Shoppers rave about using this IPL device on their face and body, including the ultra-sensitive bikini line.

Like other laser hair removal devices, this IPL tool features a manual mode that emits a single flash at a time to precisely target areas, like the chin, upper lip, and armpits. There is also an auto mode that emits continuous flashes for the legs, stomach, and arms. And FWIW, this device comes with an epic 36-month warranty and 100-day money-back policy, which is more than triple the regular return window of other Amazon beauty products.

The main complaint about this price-friendly tool is that it’s bulky, making it less ideal for travel. However, it does boast an ergonomic design for an overall comfortable hair removal experience. And since each treatment area requires a maximum of two minutes or less, you won’t have to worry about any discomfort for your wrist.

If you’re like us, then you’re probably a bit surprised that an at-home laser hair removal device can be so costly. However, we put this one to the test for nearly two months and saw major results. Based on our long-term testing experience, Epilaser’s effective tech, and the sophisticated design and feel, we knew it was deserving of a spot on this list. We adored it so much that we featured it as one of the best beauty launches of 2025 in our annual Skincare Awards package.

Our deputy visual director, Dangi McCoy, usesd this laser two to three times a week for two months on her right underarm to compare the results. She noticed the treated area regrew hair more slowly, and had half the amount of underarm hair compared to her left side. “At seven weeks, I’m still using the laser, but the regrowth has been so sparse I could count the hairs at a glance,” McCoy said in her Epilaser review.

Notably, this is the only featured device that use diode lasers for hair removal. As a quick reminder, using the wrong laser type, aka IPL, can cause burns in dark brown and deep skin tones. Thankfully, the Epilaser’s diodes prevent this from happening. The device’s unique laser wavelength bypasses the melanin that gives our skin its pigment, allowing it to safely remove hair rather than mistaking our skin for dark hair.

Epilaser is also extremely functional when you have limited outlets in your home or hotel room. During McCoy’s testing process, she found some of the cords to be cumbersome, so it was nice to have the flexibility of charging her device and using it cordless. It also allowed McCoy to remove hair from anywhere in her home, such as the couch while watching Uptown Girls.

OK, so what about the discomfort? Is splurging really worth it in this case? Turns out, yes! Epilaser maximizes hair removal results even if you have a low tolerance for discomfort. While no laser hair removal device is completely painless, McCoy only felt occasional quick pricks on her skin. The brand’s proprietary SPOT technology zaps up to 15 hairs per second, while leaving your skin untouched.

She was also impressed by how lightweight the cordless Epilaser felt in her hands. The device feels sturdy, and its ergonomic design enhances comfort during longer treatment sessions. Plus, this laser hair removal device looks absolutely gorgeous IRL—the bronze-tone trim truly elevates the luxurious appearance.

Given the laser’s smaller opening, you can even use this device on your face. It also comes with a soft-sided travel case with a short handle strap that’s easy to pack in your carry-on or rolling suitcase.

SmoothSkin's system works for anyone who wants something that's easy to use and doesn't require a lot of manual work or tinkering with buttons or various features. A patented sensor measures your skin before each flash and automatically selects the light best suited to your skin tone. This helps speed up the whole process, so full-body treatments take approximately 10 minutes.

It also includes a precision head to target smaller areas of the body—like the bikini line or even the upper lip or chin. The adaptable head also makes it easier to follow along your natural curves, like your kneecaps or underarms.

Like other great laser hair removal devices on the market, this one promises visible hair reduction in as little as four weeks and complete results by 12 weeks. It works so well that you’ll notice a difference after just one use, which is a true testament to this laser's power. SmoothSkin is on the pricey side, but justified by the fact that it offers unlimited flashes, allowing you to use this device for life. Overall, an excellent value over its lengthy lifetime. No wonder it earned 250 five-star Amazon reviews.

You've probably seen this popular laser hair removal device on your social media feeds, and our team says it really does live up to the hype. Nood’s proprietary PrecisionPulse laser makes all of the difference. The IPL flashes every 10 milliseconds, meaning it exposes your skin to less light that could accidentally cause burns.

Nood’s combination of continuous flashes and larger window make it better suited for larger areas, especially the legs. You can polish them off in 15 to 20 minutes, though it's harder to target smaller areas, like the upper lip. We also love the large digital display on this model.

It makes it very easy to toggle through the seven different intensity levels, and it's always clear which one you're working on. The price is friendlier than some other options, plus the brand offers a 90-day money-back guarantee, which makes this device a great option for anyone on the fence about at-home laser hair removal.

There are a lot of laser hair removal devices on the market, which is why you should consider a few of these pointers before investing.

IPL and diode lasers both slow hair growth and reduce the thickness of individual strands by scanning for pigment and targeting the hair follicle, says dermatologist Melanie Kingsley, MD. But, they each have their benefits and limitations.

IPL is the most commonly used type of light in at-home laser hair removal devices. This technology uses broad-spectrum light to target melanin, the pigment that gives your hair its color. The light is also unsuitable for dark and deep skin tones because it can’t distinguish between melanin-rich skin and the pigment of dark hair, says dermatologist Rachel Nazarian, MD. However, if you have a fair to olive complexion with dark hair, then you’re an ideal candidate for IPL treatments.

Until recently, all at-home laser hair removal devices were IPL lasers. But Epilaser has a game-changing laser for home use. Unlike IPL lights, which emit a broad spectrum of light ranging from 400 to 1,400 nm, diode lasers are unique because they use a more concentrated wavelength of light (around 810 nm). This precise wavelength means it can better target the hair follicles rather than accidentally burning your skin, making it more accessible for some people with darker complexions.

Both are effective, but diode lasers are slightly more versatile. That said, no matter which one you go with, you’ll need multiple treatments to maintain your hair-free results.

One of the biggest considerations is the number of flashes a device is equipped to deliver. This number indicates how long the device will last, according to Dr. Nazarian. "Many devices contain about 200,000 flashes, which is typically good for more than 15 years, although it also depends on how many areas you’re treating," she says. Other recommendations on this list, like the Smoothskin, have unlimited flashes, which means they'll theoretically last forever, but are pricier.

Extra features like multiple intensity modes—lower options for sensitive skin; higher settings for those who want to see results fast (see the Nood)—or interchangeable heads for precise treatment all over the body (hi, Braun) can increase the price. The amount you spend comes down to the features you want in your device and how long you want it to last.

One of the best ways to reduce discomfort during laser hair removal is to use cooling technology. It lowers your skin’s temperature—before, during, and after each laser pulse—to help you better tolerate longer and higher treatment settings safely.

Devices with bigger heads are more efficient on large areas. For more targeted flashes, opt for rigs with compact heads, such as the Iouniya Laser Hair Removal, which can be used on both the face and body. If you have sensitive skin, consider stretching your treatments out to once a month to start and gradually up the frequency once your skin can handle the laser hair removal treatment. The final hair-free results will take longer to achieve but at least you won’t risk irritating your skin. FWIW, she says you’ll notice thinning hair after your first four treatments.

Once you choose your device, know that it can take some time to see results. While every device is different, you’ll probably use it weekly anywhere from four to 10 weeks before noticing lasting results, says dermatologist Bertha Baum, DO. The final results might take longer to achieve, but you won’t risk irritating your skin. FWIW, warm weather likely won’t return until April or early May, meaning you’ve got several weeks to achieve smooth results. Either way, Dr. Baum says you’ll notice thinning hair after your first four treatments.

This technology has come a long way and, while pricey, it's a long-term investment that pays for itself. Think of it this way: A laser that costs $500 is basically the same price as a professional hair removal session, and that in-office treatment won't last forever, but you will continue using your at-home laser for years. And FWIW, we found a few discounted, top-rated Amazon picks that start at just $42, but you’ll want to hurry since these are fleeting deals.

At Women’s Health, we prioritize hands-on editor testing to ensure you don’t waste your time or money. Ahead is insight on what went into our editorial process while trying the latest and greatest at-home laser hair removal devices.

After testing these devices since February 2022, beauty director Brian Underwood, deputy deals and trends editor Eunice Lucero-Lee, and luxury commerce editor Sarah Maberry whittled down this list to 12 of the best laser hair removal devices. We also tapped contributors Jasmine Gomez, Lily Wohlner, and Brigitt Earley to ensure these devices work across most skin tones.

They all boast impressive features, are comfortable to use, and offer incredible value. Plus, these picks are FDA-cleared, so they’ve been evaluated for safety and efficacy. Several dermatologists also shared their no-fail laser hair removal tips and best-in-class product recommendations.

And because we know what it’s like to ball on a budget, we also considered pricing. TBH, laser hair removal devices aren’t exactly cheap. Many cost between $300 and $600, especially when shopping for these expert-approved devices from well-respected brands, such as Braun.

To help, I carefully researched dozens of other cheaper, yet top-rated Amazon laser hair removal devices. Ultimately, I found four Amazon picks that are aligned with expert guidance and are currently discounted as low as $35. Talk about major savings! For added peace of mind, they all earned thousands of rave reviews from real Amazon customers.

So if you're ready to ditch daily shaving and bi-monthly waxing, we're confident—based on our own testing and our dermatologists' advice—that this list contains only the best, most effective options on the market worth your hard-earned coins.

Dr. Nazarian confirms at-home laser hair removal devices are generally safe and effective, citing a 2019 paper. The biggest challenge with many at-home devices comes down to their inability to differentiate between dark skin and dark hair due to their pigmentation. Melanin-rich complexions risk absorbing too much laser energy that increases the risk for burning, cautions Dr. Nazarian. If this is you, then see your dermatologist for a recommendation on the best laser hair removal treatments and devices.

It's also a good idea to do a patch test and not expose the treated area to sunlight for a week, says Dr. Shirazi. Your treated skin is temporarily more sensitive, and you risk sunburn, hyperpigmentation, and delayed healing. She also doesn’t suggest using the laser on tanned and tattooed skin, open wounds, moles, or birthmarks to avoid changing their appearance or causing accidental burns.

Truthfully, they're not optimal for sensitive or dark skin. Many at-home devices cannot distinguish between melanin-rich complexions and dark hair, says dermatologist Corey L. Hartman, MD. Anyone else can still give them a try.

And, like with salon treatments, it's important to practice patience—this isn't a "one and done" situation. Many devices need to be used multiple times weekly to achieve the initial results. Plus, each at-home session can take 10 to 60 minutes, depending on how much body and facial hair you plan to remove. While a tad annoying upfront, this minor inconvenience has a major payoff because your hair will regrow slower over time with regular use.

#5083. Jensen Huang Resigns as Nvidia CEO, With CFO Colette Kress Named Interim Chief

Jensen Huang Resigns as Nvidia CEO, With CFO Colette Kress Named Interim Chief

Jensen Huang has resigned as CEO of Nvidia, ending a 33-year tenure at the helm of the chipmaker he co-founded, after reports of affairs with a suspected Chinese spy and a senior company executive.

Huang has stepped down as president, CEO and a member of the board, effective immediately, Nvidia said on Thursday. Colette Kress, Nvidia's chief financial officer since 2013, will serve as interim CEO while remaining CFO, as the board searches for a permanent successor from both inside and outside the company. Nvidia did not give a reason for Huang's resignation, but thanked him for his "immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry."

NVIDIA announces CEO transition. Read the release: https://t.co/MTTUvFHCJA

— NVIDIA Newsroom (@nvidianewsroom) November 12, 2026

The board also named Harvey Jones, a former CEO and executive chairman of chip design software company Synopsys, as its first-ever chair.

"The Board has full confidence in Colette and the leadership team, and we expect the company's operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption," Jones said.

Kress said she was "committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years." Nvidia will report its third-quarter results as scheduled on Tuesday, the company said.

Nvidia shares were down 7.7% at $160.28 shortly after the market opened on Thursday, having fallen as low as $148.80, according to Yahoo! Finance data.

Huang's departure comes four days after he acknowledged in a letter to staff that he had been unfaithful to his wife, prompting Nvidia's board to open an independent investigation. He had told the board that he had been intimate with Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based Nvidia customer Megaspeed, The New York Times reported.

The Times had reported in October that U.S. officials had concluded Alice Huang was a Chinese intelligence asset, while the Financial Times later reported that a U.S. government memo said the two had been romantically involved. China has denied the allegations.

On Wednesday, the Times reported that Huang had also had a relationship with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of health care, who reports to him. The Wall Street Journal later reported that the board was preparing to oust him, adding to the pressure on the CEO.

The scandal has wiped hundreds of billions of dollars off Nvidia's market value, with the company losing about $430 billion in two days earlier this week. Nvidia and Huang also face a proposed shareholder class action, and lawmakers had threatened to subpoena him.

Huang ran Nvidia with about 60 executives reporting directly to him and has said he did not believe in succession planning, leaving the company without an obvious successor.

Prior to the announcement of Huang's resignation, one person inside the company had told the Financial Times that naming Kress as interim CEO would be the simplest option. Other potential candidates cited by the paper's sources include Ian Buck, who runs Nvidia's data center business, and Arm CEO Rene Haas, a former Nvidia executive.

Huang remains Nvidia's largest shareholder, with a stake of about 3.6%, according to the Journal.

#5081. Unocoin halts all services after hackers bypass BitGo freeze

Unocoin says suspected misuse of backup wallet access enabled unauthorized transfers outside BitGo as the exchange investigates losses.

Crypto exchange Unocoin said on Nov. 13 that disputed wallet transfers were signed and broadcast outside BitGo, while the freeze on its BitGo enterprise account had worked so far.

The exchange suspended all services on Nov. 9 after detecting further unauthorized activity. It had requested freezes on its enterprise accounts at BitGo and Fireblocks after initially detecting the activity on Nov. 6.

In its incident update, Unocoin said a backup mechanism designed to preserve access to funds if BitGo became unavailable appeared to have been exploited. It is still investigating how that mechanism was used, cryptocurrency losses, and potential information exposure.

BitGo's wallet documentation describes three keys: the user key, backup key, and BitGo key. Normal transactions use the user and BitGo keys to meet a two-of-three signing requirement. The backup key can instead pair with either of the other two keys.

Pairing the backup key with the user key provides a signing route that does not require BitGo's key, and the two-of-three requirement still applies in that recovery arrangement.

What changes is the pair of keys used to satisfy it: the user and backup keys replace the usual user-and-provider combination, leaving BitGo outside that signing process.

BitGo notes that limit in its withdrawal-policy documentation, saying that those policies apply only to transactions involving BitGo. Recovery transactions using the user and backup keys bypass the policies configured with the provider.

The user and BitGo keys sign. BitGo participates, and its withdrawal policies apply.

This recovery capability preserves access when the provider is unavailable and helps explain why an account freeze cannot be treated as a blanket restriction on every transaction the wallet's keys can sign.

Unocoin reported identifying outgoing transactions on Nov. 12 from an Ethereum address within its BitGo wallet infrastructure used to fund ERC-20 tokens. Its Nov. 13 explanation attributes the disputed activity to external signing, while the suspected misuse of backup access remains under investigation.

In the Nov. 12 report, Unocoin said more than 90% of customer cryptocurrency funds were maintained in cold storage. It was still establishing the complete status of holdings and potential exposure, so that statement does not settle the loss assessment.

Unocoin's latest update said work to restore services continued. Unresolved questions include how the suspected recovery path was accessed, what losses or information exposure resulted, and when services can resume.

#5074. Coinbase AI trading tool pauses bots, but leaves orders open

Coinbase adds server-enforced AI trading limits and loss triggers, leaving users responsible for managing open orders and positions.

Coinbase is rolling out Agent Controls for Agents, its service that connects users' AI tools to their trading accounts.

The Nov. 11 announcement adds limits enforced on Coinbase's servers, while leaving users responsible for the trades their agents make.

On Nov. 13, CEO Brian Armstrong promoted the controls as a way to make AI use in financial accounts safe. A pause on new trades does not mean existing orders have been canceled, positions closed, or losses ended.

In its Agent Controls announcement, Coinbase describes a maximum dollar amount for each trade and a cap on total trading over 24 hours, and trades exceeding the volume limit will not go through.

Auto-stop adds a portfolio percentage-loss trigger, and the agent stops placing trades until the user turns trading back on in the Coinbase app.

Coinbase says enforcement runs on its servers, where the agent cannot bypass the limits or change them itself, while users manage the settings through their authenticated Coinbase account. That separates the rules governing execution from instructions given to an AI model.

Product-category permissions remain forthcoming. Coinbase labels the choice of whether an agent may trade crypto, equities, or derivatives as coming soon.

The announcement does not say auto-stop cancels outstanding orders or closes existing positions, and also gives no loss-calculation baseline or valuation frequency, and does not define how the 24-hour volume window is counted.

Coinbase's agent guide treats order management as a set of distinct operations, while its equity guidance warns that receiving an order ID is not proof of a fill and says individual cancellation results must be checked.

The command reference lists canceling an order and closing a position separately, with availability depending on the product.

The practical implication is that a user cannot treat an agent's stopped status as confirmation that exposure has ended. A pause, a successful cancellation, and a closed position answer different questions. The published auto-stop description supports the first of those, without promising the other two.

#5072. Tether Gold Gets Clean KPMG Audit Confirming $2.2B in Physical Gold Backing

Tether Gold Gets Clean KPMG Audit Confirming $2.2B in Physical Gold Backing

Tether's gold-backed stablecoin, Tether Gold (XAUT), has completed its first full audit by KPMG, which found the token fully backed by physical gold, the company announced on Thursday.

KPMG issued an unqualified opinion on the financial statements of TG Commodities, which issues XAUT, for the year ended December 31, 2025. An unqualified, or "clean," opinion means the auditor found that the statements fairly present the company's financial position, without reservations.

Tether Gold (XAU₮) Becomes Tether’s Second Stablecoin to Complete a Big Four AuditLearn more: https://t.co/eO0asUwvlI

As of the end of 2025, TG Commodities held 520,089.350 troy ounces of allocated gold, valued at $2.246 billion, against 520,089.300 XAUT tokens in issue, according to Tether. The gold is held in vaults in Switzerland, and each token represents an ownership interest in gold on specific bars.

As part of the audit, KPMG physically counted and inspected every gold bar backing the token, rather than relying only on confirmations from custodians, Tether said.

"KPMG counted every single bar as part of its Tether Gold audit," Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said, adding that he believes XAUT "is on track to become the first true competitor to the gold ETF market."

The XAUT audit is Tether's second by a Big Four firm. In August, KPMG issued a clean opinion on Tether International, the issuer of its flagship USDT stablecoin, in what the company called the largest inaugural audit in history, Decrypt reported at the time.

For years, Tether faced criticism for relying on quarterly attestations, which offer a snapshot of reserves at a single point in time, rather than a full audit of its finances. The company first said earlier this year that it was being audited by a Big Four firm without naming it, before confirming KPMG.

Tether still publishes quarterly attestations for USDT. Its latest, prepared by accounting firm BDO and covering the period to September 30, showed total reserve assets of $191.5 billion against $183.5 billion in liabilities, giving it an excess reserve buffer of almost $8 billion, according to the report. Tether said it made $1.5 billion in net operating profit in the third quarter.

"These milestones advance the progress towards audits across the whole of Tether," said chief financial officer Simon McWilliams.

Separately from the gold backing XAUT, Tether has also built up its own large gold reserves, and Ardoino has said it will keep adding to its stash, which it stores in a former nuclear bunker in Switzerland.

#5070. Over 35% of Bitcoin Supply Faces Potential Quantum Risk, New Data Shows

#5066. Anchorage Digital’s Stablecoins Can Now Settle Payments on Visa’s Network

Anchorage Digital’s Stablecoins Can Now Settle Payments on Visa’s Network

Anchorage Digital is extending its stablecoin reach into one of the world’s largest payment networks, teaming up with Visa to let select Anchorage-issued tokens settle transactions directly on VisaNet, starting with Western Union’s USDPT.

Under the arrangement announced Thursday, Visa and eligible companies can now use USDPT, a dollar-pegged stablecoin issued and custodied by Anchorage Digital Bank, to settle their obligations on the Visa network.

It’s the first Anchorage-issued token to gain that status, and the companies said the deal establishes a framework to add more of its stablecoins later.

The appeal, Anchorage argues, is pairing the speed of a stablecoin with the backing of a regulated bank. Anchorage operates what it bills as America’s first federally chartered crypto bank, overseen by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency.

“Speed alone won’t bring institutions onchain,” said Nathan McCauley, Anchorage’s co-founder and CEO, arguing that institutions want “a regulated institution behind the money,” now getting both a stablecoin’s speed and a federally regulated bank’s safeguards.

The move is the latest sign of Visa weaving stablecoins into its settlement plumbing.

The payments giant has built out a stablecoin settlement program spanning networks like Base, Polygon and others, launched a platform to help banks and fintech firms issue and move stablecoins, and has moved into onchain lending tied to its cards.

Dan Roesbery, a Visa vice president for crypto partnerships, framed the USDPT support as giving partners “another trusted, institution-grade option” for settling with Visa.

For Anchorage, the deal advances a broader ambition to become the settlement bank for stablecoins at institutional scale, not just issuing them but providing the custody and settlement rails underneath.

The bank already issues a roster of institution-grade stablecoins, including Tether’s U.S.-regulated USAT, Western Union’s USDPT, Ethena’s USDtb and others, each redeemable one-to-one for dollars. Its counterparty settlement network, Atlas, handles off-exchange settlement, collateral management and cross-border transfers.

Anchorage also recently positioned itself as the custody backbone of the U.S.-Mexico stablecoin corridor, custodying tokens on both sides of one of the world’s largest remittance routes. Backing a token on Visa’s network, which reaches merchants and banks worldwide, extends that institutional footprint further into mainstream payments.

The companies said support for additional Anchorage-issued stablecoins could follow the initial USDPT launch.

#5062. DOJ Wins Court Authority to Seize $1.2 Billion of North Korea’s Stolen Binance Crypto as Freezes Top $2.7 Billion

The DOJ said Thursday it has court authority to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion in cryptocurrency stolen from Binance, part of a freeze of more than $2.7 billion that officials said halted about half of North Korea’s October exchange heist.

In a Thursday announcement, the department said that on or about Oct. 29, members of the North Korean military, referred to by the FBI as TraderTraitor, stole more than $6 billion worth of virtual assets from Binance. That is below the $6.34 billion figure Binance has covered since the attack.

Binance said it had completed coverage of the assets hit in the breach, replacing the tokens from company funds rather than by recovering the stolen coins. Those are separate tracks: the DOJ is trying to interdict what was taken, while the exchange has said users were made whole from its Secure Asset Fund for Users, a portion of its futures insurance fund and its treasury.

Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the DOJ’s Criminal Division said the department and its partners were able to “immediately halt about half of this historic breach” by freezing stolen assets “before they got beyond law enforcement reach.” The freeze of more than $2.7 billion is a joint figure for U.S. government and private-sector efforts. Of that amount, the DOJ said it has already obtained court authorization to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion. The underlying court papers were not posted with the announcement.

The $1.2 billion is not newly recovered money but comes out of the roughly $2.85 billion Binance said on Nov. 3 had been frozen or intercepted, and Thursday’s court authorization is the legal step that lets the government move toward taking ownership of those funds through forfeiture, where until now they had simply been frozen at the token issuers.

Even that freeze is not the end of the trail. The DOJ said TraderTraitor actors are still moving the stolen assets through cryptocurrency bridges, mixers and exchanges, and that tracing, seizure and forfeiture work continues. Last week, on Oct. 31, the FBI, with the U.S. Secret Service and IRS Criminal Investigation, issued a Cyber Alert attributing the theft to North Korea and urging virtual asset service providers to block transactions with or derived from addresses the actors are using. The alert said investigators have seen the stolen assets converted primarily into ether.

Separately from the DOJ and Binance case, the U.S. attorney’s office in the Central District of California and the FBI announced the seizure of cloud-based infrastructure used in a social engineering campaign the FBI is calling FaceStealer. The FBI said the scheme has resulted in the theft of more than $400 million in cryptocurrency over the last 18 months and has also been used in attempts to compromise people who maintain open-source software, a step the bureau said appears calculated to enable supply-chain attacks.

The method is a fake video call. The FBI said North Korean hackers, known publicly under names including APT38 and BlueNoroff, lure targets with meeting invitations sent from accounts stolen from earlier victims. Once a target joins, the hackers play a prerecorded webcam video of a person the target knows, or a deepfake of a well-known figure in the cryptocurrency industry, then introduce a fake technical error and send a “fix” that installs malware. In several cases, the theft came months to more than a year after the first compromise, as the hackers waited for wallet balances to grow.

A Thursday FBI FLASH report said the meetings run on imposter versions of Zoom, Microsoft Teams and Google Meet, with invitations often moving through hijacked Telegram, LinkedIn, Slack or Discord accounts. Pursuant to a federal warrant, the FBI seized more than 900 webcam videos of FaceStealer victims. The bureau has posted a hub for the campaign at fbi.gov/facestealer.

Principal Deputy Assistant Attorney General for National Security M. Scott Proctor tied both Thursday’s actions to the same charge: “North Korea’s government bankrolls its rogue regime and illicit weapons program through cryptocurrency theft.”

The Binance recovery is still being run by the FBI’s Los Angeles Field Office, Cyber Division and Virtual Asset Unit, with the Secret Service and IRS-CI. The DOJ did not say how much of the more than $2.7 billion freeze, or of the $1.2 billion under court authority, is bitcoin.

#5058. Tron, Tether and Chainalysis Form a New Crypto-Crime Task Force—Replacing One That Just Collapsed

Tron, Tether and Chainalysis Form a New Crypto-Crime Task Force—Replacing One That Just Collapsed

Tron, Tether, and blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis have launched a joint effort to hunt down and disrupt criminal activity involving the USDT stablecoin, just weeks after a nearly identical alliance, with a different analytics partner, quietly fell apart.

Announced Wednesday, the Digital Crime Task Force aims to identify illicit activity involving Tether’s USDT on the Tron blockchain and surface it for law enforcement before criminals can move their funds.

The pitch is a shift from reactive to proactive: rather than waiting for a victim to report a crime or an investigator to flag tainted funds, the group says it will proactively trace criminal networks and coordinate asset freezes, drawing on Chainalysis’s intelligence and AI-powered investigative tools. It will also accept tips and freeze requests from police.

“Criminals are using AI to move faster than ever, and waiting for a victim to report a crime is no longer good enough,” said Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino, noting the company has frozen more than $7 billion tied to illicit activity while working with over 360 law enforcement agencies across 73 countries.

Tron founder Justin Sun framed it as protecting the millions who rely on USDT, which circulates on Tron to the tune of more than $94 billion.

The notable wrinkle is what this new alliance replaces. Tron and Tether previously ran a similar operation, the T3 Financial Crime Unit, formed in 2024 with rival analytics firm TRM Labs and later joined by Binance. Together, the group froze more than $450 million in tainted assets.

But Bloomberg reported earlier this month that T3 was quietly disbanded in late August, with people familiar citing slow response times and a lack of coordination among its members. Its collapse went public just days before the record $6.4 billion Binance hack.

Swapping TRM for Chainalysis is a pointed move, given the two are fierce competitors. Chainalysis has even sued the U.S. government over an ICE contract awarded to TRM without competitive bidding, underscoring the rivalry now running through crypto’s crime-fighting infrastructure.

The new task force says it will target a broad sweep of threats, from romance and investment scams to stolen funds, terrorist financing, North Korean cyber operations, cartel money laundering and child-exploitation material.

The group also framed the effort around a coming era of autonomous AI agents transacting onchain, which it warned will open fresh avenues for criminal exploitation.

#5056. How to Lose Weight Naturally, According to Experts

Here are 10 easy-to-follow tips to speed up the process—and make it more enjoyable.

Women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

Starting a weight-loss journey is no easy feat. There’s a lot to think about, between getting into a regular workout routine, changing up what you eat, and maybe even considering a GLP-1 medication.

But at its core, weight loss is about developing a healthy, sustainable relationship with food and movement. You don’t have to make a dozen changes all at once—the goal is long-term success, even if it’s a slow process. That’s why you should aim to lose one to two pounds a week, says Danielle Crumble Smith, RDN, a dietitian at Eat Well, Live Well. Working out at a manageable pace, eating balanced meals, and making maintainable changes can help you feel your best.

Meet the experts: Danielle Crumble Smith, RDN, is a nutritionist at Eat Well, Live Well. Kami Blease, CPT, is a personal trainer at Fyt Personal Training. Tatyana Johnston, CPT, is a former Nike master trainer and event specialist at Lululemon. Jordan Hill, RD, is a nutritionist with Top Nutrition Coaching.

Ahead, experts share their 10 best tips to make your weight-loss journey successful.

First, be sure to consult your doctor—they’ll help you set mindful, attainable goals that will keep your body healthy and strong. Then, try implementing more of these habits into your lifestyle:

Take the stairs every day at work or hold a quick plank first thing in the morning. "All these things add up over time," says Kami Blease, CPT, a personal trainer at Fyt Personal Training. "I recommend finding things you could do almost daily.”

Additionally, try adding a brisk 30-minute walk into your day (even if it’s broken up into three 10-minute walks) to increase calorie burn and push you closer to your weight-loss goals, per the Mayo Clinic. "It's low impact and not a super strenuous form of movement, which increases the chances that someone will stick with it,” says Tatyana Johnston, CPT, a former Nike master trainer and event specialist at Lululemon. "Just remember to recover with hydration, fuel, and stretching.”

Burn fat and build muscle with the WH+ 4-week walking plan

Strength training “helps with balance and stability, improves metabolism, and even lowers your risk of certain diseases," says Blease. Resistance training has also been found to help with weight loss and body recomposition, according to a 2026 study in Frontiers in Endocrinology that had 304 adults follow a calorie-restricted diet and either resistance train, do aerobic exercise, or no exercise for 1 to 18 months.

To get comfortable with form, try practicing bodyweight exercises first, Blease recommends, then add weights after you’ve mastered the move. This can help you focus on progressive overload—which means gradually increasing the weight, frequency, or number of reps over time, Blease says. Eventually, you should aim to work all major muscle groups at least twice a week, per the new ACSM resistance training guidelines.

Cardio can also help with weight loss—the CDC recommends 150 minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic activity (such as brisk walking) per week, or 75 minutes of vigorous-intensity activity (like running) each week. However, this number can vary based on someone’s individual health, and the intensity of the cardio. "Consistency is key. If you can establish and stick to a cardio schedule, you have a better chance at losing weight and keeping it off," Johnston says. Playing sports, working out with friends, or listening to a podcast during cardio can help boost your motivation too.

Also, if you enjoy high-impact exercises and want to lose weight fast, HIIT workouts can be a great way to expend a lot of energy in a short period of time. "You can ramp up the intensity by trying to get in more reps during a certain amount of time or using heavier weights while maintaining the same time goal,” says Blease. “Both will increase your intensity and continue to challenge your body."

If the gym or workout classes aren’t really your speed, choose a form of movement that you love so you can stay consistent with it. “Hiking, swimming, skiing, surfing, or biking are all forms of movement that might feel more sustainable,” says Blease.

"Start smaller than you might think," Blease says. "Often, people overcommit because they are excited. However, it's then easy to get burnt out." After a few weeks, add in a second day, and when that feels seamless, try a third, and over time, you'll find a cadence that works for you, she adds.

Just make sure you always have at least one rest day. "People can get so fixated on weight loss that they end up [overdoing exercise and] hurting themselves," Blease says. "Take time to stretch, rest, and recover as needed."

"Having a trainer create a program that is specific to your needs ensures that you are more likely to get the results you are looking for—and keep your body safe in the process," says Blease. They can help you lose fat while building muscle, which can better your overall metabolic health and insulin sensitivity, and regulate blood sugar to support a healthier body recomposition.

A trainer will also make sure you maintain proper form and that you stay consistent. Decide on a number of days per week that fits your goal and budget, and ask your trainer to help hold you accountable, Blease says.

Research suggests that working with a personal trainer may have more profound effects on weight loss: A 2024 study in Heliyon had 66 adults train individually, with a partner, or a personal trainer over 12 weeks, and they monitored their improvements in bench presses, squats, skeletal muscle mass, and fat mass. The group that worked with a personal trainer improved their leg training and reduced fat mass compared to the other groups.

Protein can help you stay full throughout the day, stabilize your blood sugar levels, and synthesize muscle mass, Smith says, helping with weight loss. While individual dietary needs vary, you can generally aim for 30 to 35 grams of protein per meal to help you stay full throughout the day. Some good sources include eggs, poultry, seafood, red meat, beans, peas, lentils, legumes, nuts, seeds, and soy, per the current Dietary Guidelines for Americans.

Additionally, "fiber is more slowly digested and helps keep you feeling full for a longer period,” Smith adds, recommending vegetables. Increased vegetable intake is also linked to lower blood sugar levels, lower triglycerides, and can help promote liver function. If you don't love veggies, you can also puree them and add them to a sauce or weight-loss-friendly smoothie.

Lastly, don’t forget about healthy (unsaturated) fats—which can help provide energy, per the Mayo Clinic. Try avocados, extra-virgin olive oil, nuts, seeds, soybeans, and seafood.

"Drinking enough water can help you to feel full and prevent overeating," says dietitian Jordan Hill, RD. Aim to drink about half your body weight in ounces of hydrating fluids per day.

Also, avoid sugary beverages. "Juices, sodas, and fancy coffees are often the calorie-equivalent of a meal, yet they will still leave you hungry," says Smith. "The sugar content is often more than a candy bar, which will cause blood sugar levels to rise." Instead, replace your beverages with fruit-infused water, herbal tea, or coffee with cinnamon or zero-calorie sweeteners.

Avoid foods that are high in added sugars, unhealthy fats, and empty calories, which can contribute to weight gain, says Hill: "Instead, focus on eating whole, nutrient-dense foods that will provide your body with the nutrients it needs."

Listening to your internal cues of hunger and fullness can help you control portion sizes, which can also aid weight loss. "Honoring fullness can help prevent overeating and ensure that you're not consuming more calories than your body needs," says Hill. Keeping a food journal can also help you become more mindful of what you're eating, when, and how you're feeling throughout the process of losing weight.

“When you skip meals or go too long in between meals or snacks, you get overly hungry. This makes it much more difficult to make healthy choices, and it also makes it harder to not overeat later," says Smith. Skipping meals can also result in a slower metabolism and leave you feeling fatigued, which can negatively impact your workouts both in effort and recovery.

If you struggle to eat consistent meals, Smith recommends munching on small snacks throughout the day. “Set yourself up for success by bringing healthy snacks with you when you’re away from home, so you’re not caught in a situation where you are really hungry but have no access to healthy food,” she says.

If you need extra assistance, a dietitian can analyze your diet and recommend personalized tips for how you can eat to lose weight, which may be more helpful than doing it on your own. A 2025 review of articles on weight-loss interventions provided by a dietitian for overweight and obese adults in the Journal of the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics looked at how working with a dietitian improved their health markers, as opposed to not working with one (the control group). The group that worked with a dietitian had improved weight loss, waist circumference, blood pressure, and quality of life compared to the control group.

When you encounter a setback (like when you skip a few days of workouts), it can be discouraging and all-consuming, and can cause you to fall off track. "One of the most crucial components of successfully reaching a goal is to not let setbacks ruin our progress,” says Johnston. “The setback is often not as severe as we think, and will not impact our end goal very much at all.”

Just take a breath and realize we’re all human and mistakes are normal; then move forward with your health plan in mind.

And don’t forget to be kind to yourself. Practicing self-compassion and returning to your plan will help reinforce your goal and remind you that this weight-loss journey requires patience and perseverance. "Practice giving yourself grace when [you] slip up,” Johnston says. “As long as it doesn’t become a habit, you will continue moving forward towards your goal.”
